subject.title: feat: add runtime self context config and tool

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `runtimeContext` plus the model-facing `runtime` core tool as a permanent shared contract, or require a plugin-first design using existing tool and hook seams?
rationale: This choice determines a new top-level config namespace, core tool-policy entry, prompt/session integration, and the ownership model for future provider/offload behavior; source review cannot safely infer that product direction.

options.title: Approve a narrow core v1 contract
options.body: Keep only static, opt-in, non-mutating context and inspection in core, with provider refresh, actions, and cost execution remaining plugin-owned.

options.title: Require a plugin-first redesign
options.body: Move the capability to a plugin using current extension seams and add only a narrowly justified generic core seam if that implementation identifies a concrete gap.

options.title: Pause for joint runtime design
options.body: Hold both runtime-context and execution-placement proposals until maintainers define their shared ownership and extension boundaries.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core v1 contract
recommendation.body: Keep only static, opt-in, non-mutating context and inspection in core, with provider refresh, actions, and cost execution remaining plugin-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly seeks this person's feedback on the core contract, and the decision is primarily product-boundary ownership.
